native_result.query: In the PCA on the forms of capital analyzed in hundred-year time slices, during the Younger Bronze Age (1100-500 BCE), how does the principal component value of PC1 in the beginning of the period at 1100 BCE differ from the subsequent time horizons between 1000 to 500 BCE?
native_result.HypoA: The beginning of the Younger Bronze Age (1100 BCE) is associated with negative values on the first principal component (PC1), while the majority of time horizons (1000-500 BCE) are characterized by positive values on PC1. This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: The PCA on the forms of capital in hundred-year time slices during the Younger Bronze Age (1100-500 BCE) shows that PC1 at the beginning of the period, 1100 BCE, is a marked positive outlier relative to every subsequent YBA slice and the y-axis can be interpreted as a general 'accumulated/intensive capital' axis (positive loadings on Hatchets/Swords, Daggers, House Size, Copper+Gold, Monument Count, Depot and Monument Size; ZSichel and ZKeform are constant in YBA and were dropped). PC1(1100 BCE) = +5.35 (YBA-only PCA, 62.5% variance) vs. PC1 mean over 1000-500 BCE = -0.89, a difference of +6.24 units or about +6.9 SD; the 1100 BCE value is +5.38 above the next-highest YBA score (1000 BCE = -0.03). A robustness PCA on all 39 slices (4300-500 BCE, PC1 = 30.3% variance) confirms the same pattern in scale: PC1(YBA subset) falls from 4.45 at 1100 BCE to 2.15 at 1000 BCE and to 0.78 by 500 BCE. Therefore 1100 BCE is a peak (terminal for the prior OBA-era configuration), followed by a single-century step-down to 1000 BCE and then a continued gradual decline through 500 BCE; the opening YBA horizon differs from the rest of the YBA span by being substantially and statistically extremely higher on PC1, with the difference dominated by the 1100->1000 BCE break.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded data/capital.csv (European-decimal commas inside quoted fields) with pandas; parsed numbers; filtered to YBA rows (BCE 500..1100, 7 slices); dropped zero-within-YBA-variance features (ZSichel, ZKeform); standardised features (z-score within the analysis window); ran PCA via SVD on the centred/scaled matrix (scipy.linalg.svd); oriented PC1 sign so that higher PC1 = higher capital; recorded loadings and per-slice scores; compared PC1 at 1100 BCE with the 1000-500 BCE subset (mean, min, max, std, excess, z-score). Repeated the full pipeline as a robustness check using all 39 rows from capital.csv (4300-500 BCE) and showed the YBA subset of that PCA. Persisted outputs to analysis/pca_yba_results.json. The full script is at analysis/pca_yba.py.
